steps.title: Import TypeScript modules for OpenAPI parsing and file operations
steps.instruction: Import the required modules: fs/promises for file operations, path for path manipulation, and yaml for YAML parsing.
steps.hint: Use import statements at the top of your TypeScript file. Remember to use the correct module names: 'fs/promises', 'path', and 'yaml'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The file will have import statements for fs/promises, path, and yaml modules at the top.
successCriteria: fs/promises, path, and yaml modules are imported using valid TypeScript import statements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported all the required modules for file operations, path manipulation, and YAML parsing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some modules, but not all. Make sure to import fs/promises, path, and yaml.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import fs/promises, path, and yaml modules.

steps.title: Define the OpenAPISpec interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named OpenAPISpec with properties for openapi, info, paths, and components.
steps.hint: Start with 'interface OpenAPISpec {' and add each property with its type. Use string for openapi and info, and Record<string, any> for paths and components.
steps.seedCode:
// Import the required modules here

// Define the OpenAPISpec interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an OpenAPISpec interface that defines the basic structure of an OpenAPI specification.
successCriteria: An interface named OpenAPISpec is defined with properties openapi (string), info (any), paths (Record<string, any>), and components (Record<string, any>).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the OpenAPISpec interface with the required properties.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined an interface, but it's missing some required properties. Make sure to include openapi, info, paths, and components.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface is not defined correctly. Please define an interface named OpenAPISpec with the specified properties.

steps.title: Define the Operation interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named Operation with properties for summary (string), description (string), parameters (array of any), and responses (object).
steps.hint: Create an interface using the 'interface' keyword followed by the name 'Operation' and define the required properties with their types.
steps.expectedOutcome: An Operation interface is created with the specified properties and types.
successCriteria: The Operation interface is defined with summary (string), description (string), parameters (any[]), and responses (Record<string, any>) properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the Operation interface with all required properties.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that all properties (summary, description, parameters, responses) are included with correct types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Operation interface is not correctly defined. Make sure to use the 'interface' keyword and include all required properties with proper TypeScript types.

steps.title: Define the ClientFunction interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named ClientFunction with properties: name (string), method (string), path (string), and parameters (array of strings).
steps.hint: Create an interface with the specified properties and their types. Remember to use proper TypeScript syntax with colons for type annotations.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ClientFunction interface is defined with the correct property types.
successCriteria: The interface ClientFunction exists with properties name: string, method: string, path: string, and parameters: string[].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the ClientFunction interface with all required properties and correct types.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Check that all four properties (name, method, path, parameters) are defined with the correct TypeScript types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ClientFunction interface is not properly defined. Make sure to create an interface with the exact property names and types specified.

steps.title: Create the parseOpenAPIFile function
steps.instruction: Create an async function named parseOpenAPIFile that takes a filePath parameter of type string and returns a Promise<OpenAPISpec>.
steps.hint: Use the async keyword before function, specify the parameter type, and declare the return type as Promise<OpenAPISpec>. The function body can be empty for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have an async function declaration with the correct signature that can later be implemented to read and parse OpenAPI files.
successCriteria: The parseOpenAPIFile function is declared as async, takes a string parameter named filePath, and returns Promise<OpenAPISpec>.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the parseOpenAPIFile function with the correct TypeScript signature. This establishes the foundation for reading OpenAPI specification files.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function is declared as async, has the filePath parameter with type string, and returns Promise<OpenAPISpec>.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Create an async function called parseOpenAPIFile that accepts a string parameter and returns Promise<OpenAPISpec>.

steps.title: Create the extractOperations function
steps.instruction: Create a function named extractOperations that takes an OpenAPISpec object as a parameter and returns an array of ClientFunction objects.
steps.hint: Define the function with proper TypeScript typing for the parameter and return type. The function body can return an empty array for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a function named extractOperations that accepts an OpenAPISpec and returns a ClientFunction array.
successCriteria: The extractOperations function is defined with correct parameter and return types.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the extractOperations function with proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the function, but check the parameter type or return type. It should accept OpenAPISpec and return ClientFunction[].
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is missing or has incorrect structure. Create a function named extractOperations that takes OpenAPISpec and returns ClientFunction[].

steps.title: Create the generateClientCode function
steps.instruction: Create a function named generateClientCode that takes an array of ClientFunction objects as a parameter and returns a string of TypeScript code.
steps.hint: Define the function with a parameter typed as ClientFunction[] and a return type of string. You can start by returning an empty string for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: A generateClientCode function is defined with the correct signature.
successCriteria: The generateClientCode function exists, accepts a ClientFunction[] parameter, and returns a string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the generateClientCode function with the correct TypeScript signature.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the function takes a ClientFunction[] parameter and returns a string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is missing or has incorrect parameters or return type. Review the expected signature.

steps.title: Create the writeClientFile function
steps.instruction: Create an async function named writeClientFile that takes two parameters: outputPath (string) and code (string), and writes the code to the file system using the fs module's writeFile.
steps.hint: Use the fs module's writeFile function with await. Remember to handle the async operation properly.
steps.expectedOutcome: The writeClientFile function is defined and ready to be used for writing generated client code to a file.
successCriteria: The writeClientFile function is declared as async, takes outputPath (string) and code (string) parameters, and uses fs.writeFile to write the code to the file system.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the writeClientFile function. This function will handle writing the generated client code to a file.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the function is async, takes the correct parameters, and properly uses fs.writeFile.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function doesn't match the requirements. Check that it's async, has the right parameters, and uses fs.writeFile correctly.

steps.title: Create the main generateClient function
steps.instruction: Create an async function named generateClient that takes two string parameters: inputPath and outputPath. Inside the function, call parseOpenAPIFile with inputPath, then pass the result to extractOperations, then pass that result to generateClientCode, and finally call writeClientFile with the generated code and outputPath.
steps.hint: Remember to use await for the async function calls and handle the data flow from parsing to writing.
steps.expectedOutcome: The generateClient function is defined and orchestrates the entire client generation process by calling the four helper functions in sequence.
successCriteria: The generateClient function is declared as async, takes inputPath and outputPath parameters, and calls parseOpenAPIFile, extractOperations, generateClientCode, and writeClientFile in the correct order.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main orchestration function that ties all the components together.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the function is async, takes the correct parameters, and calls all four helper functions in sequence.
steps.feedbackWrong: The generateClient function is missing or incorrect. It should be an async function that orchestrates the entire client generation process.

steps.title: Add error handling to the main function
steps.instruction: Wrap the logic inside the generateClient function in a try-catch block to handle errors gracefully.
steps.hint: Place the existing function body inside a try block, and add a catch block to handle any errors that occur.
steps.expectedOutcome: The generateClient function will now handle errors by catching them and logging an error message instead of crashing.
successCriteria: The generateClient function contains a try block with the existing logic and a catch block that logs an error.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added error handling to the generateClient function. This ensures the function handles failures gracefully.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the entire function body is inside the try block and you have a catch block to handle errors.
steps.feedbackWrong: The generateClient function should have a try-catch block. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Export the main function and interfaces
steps.instruction: Export the generateClient function and all three interfaces (OpenAPISpec, Operation, ClientFunction) from the module using named exports.
steps.hint: Add export statements before each interface definition and the generateClient function declaration.
steps.expectedOutcome: The module will export the main generateClient function and all three interfaces, making them available for import in other TypeScript files.
successCriteria: The generateClient function and all three interfaces (OpenAPISpec, Operation, ClientFunction) are exported using named exports.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully exported the main function and interfaces, completing your typed OpenAPI client generator skeleton.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've exported some items, but make sure to export all three interfaces and the generateClient function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The exports are missing or incorrect. Remember to use named exports for all three interfaces and the generateClient function.
